deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §6/§7 of Riemann's 1851 Inauguraldissertation. It states and proves the plane integral theorem (Green's theorem) for a possibly multi-sheeted surface T spread over the plane A, and then introduces boundary coordinates (s, p). The previous folio sets up the proof. T is cut into strips parallel to the y-axis, each over an element dx of the x-axis. Every branch point lies on a cutting line, so each strip consists of separate trapezoidal pieces. Lower endpoints are O_, O_,, ...; upper endpoints are O', O'', .... X takes the values X_, ... and X', ... there, and ds_, ..., ds', ... are the boundary elements cut out by the strip.

(1) Strip integral. By the fundamental theorem of calculus on each vertical segment,
∫ ∂X/∂y dy = -X_, - X_,, - ... + X' + X'' + ....

(2) Projection of boundary elements. Let the angle in question be the angle between the inward normal and the y-axis; this is η in the statement on the next page. That angle is acute at the lower endpoints and obtuse at the upper endpoints. The page says the angles are 'spitz' at the lower endpoints; 'stumpf' at the upper ones is implied by the signs. Hence
dx = cos(angle)_, ds_, = cos(angle)_,, ds_,, = -cos(angle)' ds' = -cos(angle)'' ds''.

(3) Substitution gives
dx ∫ ∂X/∂y dy = -Σ X cos(angle) ds,
summed over all boundary elements whose projection is dx.

(4) Integrating over all dx exhausts T and its boundary:
∫ ∂X/∂y dT = -∫ X cos η ds.

(5) Similarly, with horizontal strips,
∫ ∂Y/∂x dT = -∫ Y cos ξ ds.

(6) Subtracting:
∫ (∂X/∂y - ∂Y/∂x) dT = ∫ (Y cos ξ - X cos η) ds,
where ξ and η are the angles of the inward normal with the x- and y-axes. This is exactly the statement on the next page. A struck-out line on the page shows an earlier sign arrangement.

(7) Boundary coordinates. s is arc length from a fixed starting point on each boundary component. p is the distance along the inward normal at the boundary point O_0. Near the boundary, x and y are functions of (s, p). On the boundary:
∂x/∂p = cos ξ, ∂y/∂p = cos η, ∂y/∂s = ±cos ξ, ∂x/∂s = ∓cos η.
The upper signs hold if the direction of increasing s makes with p the same angle as the y-axis makes with the x-axis, i.e. (p, s) is oriented like (x, y). Riemann fixes this orientation, so that
∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s and hence ∂y/∂p = -∂x/∂s.
The Jacobian ∂(x,y)/∂(p,s) = cos²ξ + cos²η = 1. In modern terms, the tangent is the inward normal rotated by +90°, i.e. the interior lies to the right of the direction of travel.

(8) Margin remarks. Reversing this direction only multiplies all s-derivatives and s-integrations by -1. Boundary integrals ∫ ... ds are unaffected, since their elements are always taken positive. The margin also notes that the differential of s equals the line element ds up to sign.

Purpose: this sets up the identity in the form later used in the dissertation, ∫(∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y) dT = -∫(X ∂x/∂p + Y ∂y/∂p) ds. That form feeds Green-type identities for harmonic u, the mean-value property, and the Dirichlet-principle arguments of §§8–18.
errors: As transcribed, the angle letters are interchanged. In the strip argument for ∫∂X/∂y the relevant angle is that of the inward normal with the y-axis (η on the next page), so ∫∂X/∂y dT = -∫X cos η ds. The final line should read ∫(∂X/∂y - ∂Y/∂x) dT = ∫(Y cos ξ - X cos η) ds, as on the next page. The page likely uses a different or ambiguous letter (it looks like ζ) and the transcription normalised it wrongly; the mathematics is fine once the letters are consistent.

The transcription 'spitz an den unteren und den oberen Endpunkten' cannot be right. The signs dx = cos(angle)_, ds_, = -cos(angle)' ds' require acute angles at the lower and obtuse angles at the upper endpoints.

The margin formula ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p contradicts the convention adopted in the main text (∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s implies ∂x/∂s = -∂y/∂p). Either a minus sign is lost in the transcription, or it is a draft written before the orientation was fixed.

Unjustified but standard for the period: the argument assumes each vertical line meets the boundary in finitely many points and that boundary elements project nondegenerately (vertical boundary pieces and tangencies are ignored). This is acceptable at the rigor level of 1851.

results.what: ∫∫_T (∂X/∂y - ∂Y/∂x) dT = ∫_∂T (Y cos ξ - X cos η) ds (inward normal), proved by slicing T into strips parallel to the axes; valid on a multi-sheeted (Riemann) surface with branch points placed on the cutting lines
results.modern_name: Green's theorem in the plane (curl/flux form), extended to Riemann surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: G. Green (1828); also Gauss, Ostrogradsky (1826/1831), Cauchy (1846); the formulation on branched surfaces is Riemann's 1851 dissertation §7

results.what: Boundary coordinates (s, p) with ∂x/∂p = cos ξ, ∂y/∂p = cos η, ∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s, ∂y/∂p = -∂x/∂s under the chosen orientation; reversing the orientation changes the sign of s-derivatives only
results.modern_name: Frenet-type normal/tangent (collar) coordinates near the boundary; orientation convention for the boundary
results.usually_credited_to: standard; appears in Riemann's published dissertation (1851)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of §§6–7 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation (Green's theorem on a surface spread over the plane, plus the s, p boundary coordinates). Both are well known as his and routine. Only minor drafting variants (the curl-form statement, letter and sign slips) differ from the printed text.

transcription_corrections: First line: the angle symbol is likely η (angle of the normal with the y-axis), or a letter resembling ζ, not ξ. The ξ/η letters in the strip derivation and the final formula appear interchanged by the transcriber. Compare the next page's statement ∫(dX/dy - dY/dx)dT = ∫(Y cos ξ - X cos η)ds.
'Die Winkel ... werden offenbar spitz an den unteren und den oberen Endpunkten' should read approximately 'spitz an den unteren und stumpf an den oberen Endpunkten'.
The margin formula ∂x/∂s = ∂y/∂p probably reads ∂x/∂s = -∂y/∂p, consistent with the adopted convention ∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s. Verify against the image.
In the struck/inserted passage near the end, the intended text is 'so annehmen, daß ∂x/∂p = ∂y/∂s und folglich ∂y/∂p = -∂x/∂s', as in the printed dissertation.
